title: The Miracles of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The miracles of Christ are His works of divine power that reveal His identity, authority, compassion, and kingdom mission. They are signs that point beyond themselves to who Jesus is and what He came to do.
summary: The miracles of Christ are His works of divine power that reveal His identity, authority, compassion, and kingdom mission. They are signs that point beyond themselves to who Jesus is and what He came to do.
christFocus: Jesus’ miracles reveal Him as the Son of God with authority over sickness, nature, demons, sin, death, and creation. They call people to faith in Him, not mere fascination with power.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The miracles of Jesus display divine authority. He commands storms, heals disease, casts out demons, multiplies food, opens blind eyes, and raises the dead. Creation obeys His voice.

His miracles are also acts of compassion. Jesus does not use power for entertainment or self-promotion. He moves toward real suffering while revealing the nearness of God’s kingdom.

The miracles point to His identity and mission. John says these signs were written so readers may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in His name.

The miracles also preview restoration. They show that sin, sickness, demons, death, and broken creation are not final. Christ is Lord over all, and His kingdom brings life where the fall has brought ruin.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People can become fascinated with miracles while missing Christ. Scripture does not present signs as spiritual entertainment, but as witnesses to the Savior.

This doctrine strengthens hope without encouraging sensationalism. Jesus has authority over every broken thing, and His miracles point to the final restoration He will bring.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let the miracles of Christ lead you to worship, faith, and hope in Him. Do not chase signs while neglecting the Savior. Trust His authority, receive His compassion, and look forward to the day when He makes all things new.
